_comment: Rules for `pmmod strings fasttext`. Each rule matches text in the client's own dumps by regex, by explicit id, or both. A match is replaced with `replace`: "skip" writes {09}, an argument slot the client never fills anywhere in its 30,341-entry corpus, so the message resolves to nothing and its box is skipped outright; "blank" writes an escaped newline pair, which still renders a box you have to dismiss. Default is skip. Keep rules narrow: silencing a prompt still shows its Yes/No box, but silencing quest directions loses information you may need.
_replace_comment: "skip" writes {09}, "blank" writes an escaped newline pair, "none" writes an empty override, and the default is skip. Which one removes a box -- or whether any of them can -- is a property of the call site, and it is not visible in the dumps. Settled on hardware 2026-08-30: at table 8, the field moves, {09} removes the box outright. At the battle tables 14/15/157/172 nothing removes it. {09} leaves an empty box that still costs a tap and drags the battle out; an empty override is read as no override at all and the vanilla text comes back. The four battle-flow rules are disabled for that reason. Do not re-enable them expecting a different token to help; the only non-argument codes in the whole corpus are DELAY_0F/14/3C/5A/64.

SupersSpeedStrings silences exactly these two with {09}, in this archive, which is the proof that the skip token works here.

rules.name: exp-gained-ds
rules.note: EXP gained at the end of a battle, live client
rules._note2: Blank, not {09}, and the difference is the whole point. {09} is an argument placeholder the battle engine never resolves: on hardware it left a box that sat there and dragged the end of the fight out. An escaped newline pair is a well-formed empty message and the engine moves through it. SupersSpeedStrings writes exactly this at exactly these two addresses and is run by thousands of people; that is the evidence, and it beats reasoning from the dumps, which is how 1.3 through 1.6 got this wrong.

rules._note2: The client does not have a string per move out here. Battle's own `{1C} {1D} used {16}!` is NOT in this list: in a battle you want to read which move was used.
rules._note3: Three ids left this rule on 2026-09-02, reported from hardware: 16804105 (`{00} used {01}! (PP Remaining: {02}/{03})`), 6060 (`You have used {00}.`) and 6087 (`You have used {00} {01}(s).`). None of them is a ROM message box. They are the client's own one-line notices -- the field-move toast and the item toast -- and 6060 is the only thing that tells you a Repel took effect, which is why using one went silent. SupersSpeedStrings silences none of the three, and it is the mod this one is measured against: it removes the box and keeps the notice. The GBA ids that stay here have never been observed on screen at all; 1.2 silenced them and the messages still drew.
rules._note4: 16780155 -- `{00}'s summoned {02} used {03}!` -- is the box, reported from hardware 2026-09-02 with Teleport and Sweet Scent. It is not a ROM message at all: PokeMMO summons the Pokemon in the overworld and writes this line itself, which is why silencing table 8 in every archive and matching every GBA `used` string never touched it. The reference silences exactly this id with {09} and nothing else in the family, which is what makes a field move look instant there. The `summoned` word is the tell -- no other entry in the corpus reads `{00}'s summoned`.

rules.note: Nurse Joy / healing counter flow
rules.match: restore your tired|We hope to see you again|Welcome to our POK|Thank you for waiting|We've restored your|take your (POK[^ ]*MON|Pok[eé]mon)(\\n| )for(\\n| )a(\\n| )few seconds|Your (POK[^ ]*MON|Pok[eé]mon) are fighting fit|welcome to\\nthe (POK[^ ]*MON|Pok[eé]mon) CENTER|restored your (POK[^ ]*MON|Pok[eé]mon)\\nto full health|We hope to see you again!
rules._exclude_note: The Safari Zone sign-out desk borrows the Pokecenter farewell; it fires once per Safari run, and the ball count it reports is worth reading.
rules._note2:
The nurse's `I'll take your Pokemon for a few seconds` wraps at a different word in each archive -- `POKeMON for a
few seconds`, `POKeMON
for a few seconds`, `Pokemon for
a few seconds` -- so every separator in the phrase has to allow the escaped newline. A plain space missed three archives, and the parity suite could not report it because its scope regex did not recognise the reference's section name for them either.
rules._note3: Both spellings are matched everywhere the name appears. The GBA tables shout `POKeMON`; the NDS archives write `Pokemon`. Spelling it only one way covered half the game and looked like full coverage.

rules.name: mart
rules.note: Shop clerk purchase and sale flow
rules.match: Anything else\?|Here you are! Thank you|Thank you very much!|Welcome!\\nHow may I serve you|Please come again|How many would you like|How may I serve you|May I help you\?
rules._exclude_note: The Hoenn Blend Master thanks you in the clerk's exact words; he is story flavour, not a counter.
rules._exclude_note2: Two Unova NPCs close on the clerk's own `Please come again`: the Driftveil gate guard reporting that Clay is busy, and the Opelucid route announcer. Both are directions, not a counter.

rules.name: daycare
rules.note: Day-care deposit, retrieval and egg hand-off
rules.match: DAY.?CARE|Take good care of it|found an EGG|got an EGG|raise one of\\nyour POK|We can raise|received the EGG|took back \{|look after your(\\n)? ?\{02\}|raise your \{02\}|Come see me in a while|can only be doing|Here's your POK
rules._exclude_note: NPCs who talk *about* the Day Care rather than run it. They use the counter's own words and are read once, not hundreds of times.
rules._note_regions: 1833017 (Kanto) and 271131465 (Hoenn) are `Which POKeMON should we raise for you?`, the same prompt this rule silences in Sinnoh at 547/16. The prose match missed them because they carry no word the pattern looks for. Found on 2026-09-01 by `tools/region_parity.py`, which groups all 166,867 entries by text and diffs each group against itself. The same line was already silenced in another region, so this was a hole, not a decision.

rules.name: fishing
rules.note: Rod cast results
rules.match: Not even a nibble|Looks like there's nothing here|A bite!|Oh! A bite

rules.name: shop-extra
rules.note: Remaining shop counter lines
rules._note2: `Thank you.` is anchored to its own line and the rule is capped at 90 characters. Unanchored and uncapped it silenced Mr. Fuji, Lorelei and Wally, none of whom are a shop counter.
rules.exclude: waiting in|looking forward to|return your Pok|You are really great
rules._note3: `Is that OK?` was removed in 1.3. It is not a shop phrase: across the dumps it matched 44 entries and almost all of them are the confirmation on a destructive or branching choice -- `The message will be lost.`, `If the leader drops out, the group will be disbanded.`, `Held items will be put in the Bag.`, `It will forget the saying it now knows.`, `You must save the game before I show you in.` The shop lines it did catch are price prompts, which this mod keeps visible on purpose anyway. The excludes cover the Black City / White Forest recruiters and the Dreamyard gift, who all close on `Thank you.`
rules._note4: `You are really great.` is a trainer's post-battle line in table 189, not a counter. Same over-reach as the Black City recruiters: the rule anchors on `Thank you.` and anything that closes on it gets caught.

rules.name: catch-flow
rules.note: Ball throw result -- fires on every encounter you throw at
rules.match: Gotcha!|was caught!|The (POK[^ ]*MON|Pok[eé]mon) broke free|Aww! It appeared to be caught|popped out of the
rules._plain_only_why: plain_only since 2026-08-30. This pattern was written for the GBA ids and it was reaching the NDS battle engines by accident -- Sinnoh table 368 and Johto table 197 are those archives' equivalent of Unova 14/15 -- writing {09} into a state machine, which is exactly what hung a wild encounter that day. It also cannot tell a move tutor's copy of a message from the battle engine's. Where the NDS equivalent is worth silencing it is hand-picked with evidence: `move-learn-result-ds` for Unova 157/38-41. Note this mod does not silence catching or evolving in Unova either, so silencing them in Sinnoh and Johto was inconsistent as well as risky.

rules._note2: Was a bare `REPEL`, which caught nine NPCs who merely mention the item, including a quiz question. The re-apply prompt (id 6012, `{00} has worn off.\nUse another?`) is deliberately left alone: silencing it leaves a naked Yes/No on a choice that wastes an item if you get it wrong.

never: raising its |Raises the |Raises evasion|Raises |Lowers |lowers the |inflict damage|inflicts |An item to be held|An attack move|A Pok[eé] Ball|Use it to flee|It is designed|restores? \d|An item for use on a POK|The user |A move that|has been hurt by|A \w+-type move
_never_comment: Global guard on regex rules only; an id listed by hand is a decision already made and is not second-guessed. Item and move descriptions are read on purpose, never mashed through -- 966 entries and ~96k characters in this corpus. No pattern may silence them, however tempting the volume. `An attack move`, `inflicts ` and `has been hurt by` were added in 1.2 after `hurt by` in status-battle silenced seven of them.
_never_label_comment: Second global guard, patterns only. A short entry with no sentence-ending punctuation is a UI label -- 'BATTLE FACTORY', 'Sweet Scent', 'Super Repel', 'Fossil' -- not a message. Silencing one blanks a menu entry rather than skipping a box, and the `never` guard above does not catch it because labels read nothing like a description.
_never_ds_tables_comment: (archive_type, region_id, table) triples in the NDS battle engine. Third global guard, patterns only. A box drawn by these tables cannot be removed by anything the strings side has -- proven on hardware 2026-08-30 -- so silencing one trades a readable line for an empty box that costs the same tap and drags the battle out. The guard exists because disabling the battle-flow rules was not enough: `catch-flow` still reached 15/65 (`Gotcha! {00} was caught!`), `evolution` still reached all of table 172, and `move-learned` still reached 157/41 and 14/688-690. Those rules were written for the GBA ids and found the Unova archive by accident. Unova table 184 is here too: it is 942 entries of trainer battle dialogue, and `mart` was matching two of them as shop lines. Table 8 is deliberately absent: it is the field-move table, the one call site where {09} does remove the box. Until 2026-09-01 this list named the Unova archive alone, which is only where the accidents had happened so far -- the other regions ship the same battle engine and were unguarded. `tools/region_parity.py` derived the twins from the corpus itself: Unova 13 (per-move `{00} used {01}!`, 1,680 entries, never guarded even in Unova) maps to Sinnoh 0 and Johto 3; Unova 14, 15 and 172 are merged into the single table Sinnoh 368 / Johto 197; Unova 157 maps to Sinnoh 453 / Johto 300. Nothing was being silenced in any of them, so this guard changes no output today -- it closes the hole a future pattern would fall into. Unova 184 has no reliable twin (Sinnoh 441 and Johto 287 share three lines with it) and is left alone rather than guessed at. Unova 204 is here from 2026-09-01. It reads like an NPC counter -- it has POWER/ACCURACY/PP/TEACH menu labels and a Heart Scale exchange -- and on 2026-09-01 a tutor rule was written for it on exactly that reasoning. `test_only_proven_addresses_are_silenced_in_a_battle_engine` refused it, and the test is right: 204 is the move relearner's copy of the move-learn state machine, and the move-learn machine is the one place hardware already proved {09} does not work -- 157/38, 40 and 41 all had to become a blank line. The same reasoning that looks sound here is the reasoning that shipped 1.9. It stays fenced until somebody relearns a move with a build that touches it.
